senses.definition: To save data somewhere it will survive a restart or a refresh.
senses.caution: Engineers hear a promise that the data will survive a crash, so do not use it for data held only in memory. With non-technical people, say save instead.
senses.example: Right now the session only lives in memory. If the pod restarts we lose the whole conversation, so we need to persist it.

cues.text: A prototype loses everything the user typed the moment the browser is refreshed, and you are writing the ticket for what has to change.
In a design review someone is holding session state in memory on a single node, and you want to name the missing property before it goes near production.
An architect asks where the agent's conversation history lives after a pod restarts, and you want the verb for putting it somewhere that survives one.

distractors: To turn an object in memory into bytes that can be sent over a wire.
To replace a running component without stopping the system around it.
To make a bad situation worse.
To avoid something deliberately and on principle.
To settle which of two possible readings is the one meant.

senses.definition: The ability of stored data to survive a restart, or the part of a system that does this.
senses.caution: Engineers hear a promise that data survives a crash or restart, so check that it really does. With non-technical people, say storage or saving instead.
senses.example: The agent forgets everything between sessions because we never added persistence for the conversation history.

cues.text: A prototype forgets every user's settings each night when the server restarts, and you are naming the missing capability.
In an architecture review you ask which component is responsible for keeping agent memory across deployments.
A vendor's chatbot demo looks great, but you ask what happens to the conversation history if their service restarts.

distractors: The practice of keeping a copy of data in memory so repeated reads are fast.
The process of turning an object in memory into bytes that can be sent over a network.
The time it takes for a request to travel from the user to the server and back again to them.
A record of every change made to a system, kept so that problems can be traced afterwards.
The practice of deleting old data on a schedule so storage costs stay under control.
